newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers see 96 PSBR overshoot, slow growth.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers see 96 PSBR overshoot, slow growth.

text.p: Employers' federation Confindustria said it expected Italy's budget deficit would be close to 130 trillion lire this year against a government forecast of a deficit somewhere between 113 trillion and 123 trillion lire.

In a regular report, Confindustria also predicted that economic growth in 1997 would be nearer to one percent rather than the two percent targeted by the Treasury. "The 1996 deficit will be close to 130 trillion lire in 1996 causing a negative knock-on effect to 1997 accounts," the report said.
The report blamed fiscal tightening in the 1997 budget for the projected slower-than-forecast growth.
The government has said the 1997 budget will cut the ratio between Italy's deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) to 3.1 percent next year.
Confindustria agreed that the 62.5 trillion lire package would improve state finances but said that even if it were entirely successful it would only cut the deficit to GDP ratio to 3.6 percent.
The ratio is forecast to be around 6.1 percent this year.

Confindustria added that many of the budget measures were shrouded in mystery. "It is still not certain how some 36.5 trillion lire of this money will be raised," the report said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
